name: harmonic oscillator, implicit midpoint rule as a kernel

claims.why: z' = (I - hA/2)^-1 (I + hA/2) z for A = [[0, 1], [-w^2, 0]] (solved by hand: det(I - hA/2) = 1 + h^2 w^2/4); the Cayley transform of A preserves the quadratic invariant. The temporary qn keeps the update simultaneous: p reads the old q
TRAP: the energy with one sign flipped (the Lagrangian, not the Hamiltonian)
true (H is exactly conserved), but the order check takes polynomial maps only and this one divides by 4 + h^2 w^2
